editorial:
You get a wild mix of grief, science, and citywide panic when a grieving marine biologist is pulled back into shark hunting after a giant predator appears in the Seine. The movie keeps things moving with tense water scenes, political pressure, and a race to stop a disaster before a major Paris event. It is not trying to be deep; it wants to give you big shark thrills, quick scares, and a few emotional beats about loss and responsibility.

The action is the main draw, with solid pacing and some strong set pieces, though the story can feel familiar and a few characters make frustrating choices. If you enjoy creature features and do not mind silly science, you will have fun.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Sophia and the rescue team lure the giant shark into the flooded catacombs and set off explosives to stop it. The blast seems to end the threat, but the twist reveals the shark was pregnant and had already released many babies into the water. As Paris floods, those young sharks spread through the streets, turning one monster into a citywide nightmare. You are left with the feeling that saving Paris has only just begun.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves shark thrillers and big disaster action.
